table_name: Carbonate System Equations, Constants, and Software
revision: R1 (2026-08-24): per-row constants policy for cold water (no silent extrapolation of Lueker constants below 2 C); zone-specific Lee et al. (2006) TA equations added; precipitation-risk framework made tiered and particle-context dependent
description: Equilibrium constants and formulations used to compute the ocean carbonate system. All chemistry columns in the dataset are deterministic outputs of these equations, not sampled values.

key_derived_quantities.potential_uptake: DIC_eq(TA0 + dose, pCO2_atm) - DIC_eq(TA0, pCO2_atm)  [thermodynamic; against the untreated counterfactual equilibrated to the same atmosphere]
key_derived_quantities.realized_uptake: f x potential_uptake  [f = kinetic equilibration fraction, a sampled input]
key_derived_quantities.thermo_efficiency_eta: potential_uptake / dose  [mol CO2 per mol TA; thermodynamic OUTPUT, expected ~0.75-0.85 per literature; never confused with f]
key_derived_quantities.state_2_chemistry: DIC2 = DIC0 + f x (DIC_eq - DIC0); then pH2, Omega2, and speciation recomputed from (TA1, DIC2)
key_derived_quantities.marginal_efficiency: Finite difference of POTENTIAL uptake between adjacent dose levels within the same environment draw, so f cannot contaminate the diminishing-returns analysis

components.component: K1, K2 (carbonic acid dissociation) - primary set
components.formulation: function of temperature and salinity, total pH scale; used ONLY inside its calibrated domain (T approx. 2-35 C, S approx. 19-43)

components.component: K1, K2 - low-temperature alternative set (rows with T < 2 C)
components.formulation: Alternative PyCO2SYS constants option whose documented validity extends below 2 C; candidate Millero (2010), final choice confirmed against stated validity ranges in the PyCO2SYS documentation at implementation time. Every row records its formulation in a constants_set column; the two sets are never mixed silently; the full dataset is re-run under the alternative set as a sensitivity case
components.source: candidate: Millero (2010); polar K1/K2 uncertainty caution: Sulpis et al. (2020) - to verify

components.formulation: numerical d(ln pCO2) / d(ln DIC) at constant total alkalinity

components.component: Baseline total alkalinity from salinity and temperature
components.formulation: Zone-specific regional equations TA = f(S, T) with published validity domains; archetype-to-zone mapping documented in environment_archetypes.json; coefficients transcribed from the paper and unit-tested against published example values. Coastal archetype uses a two-end-member mixing line; marginal-sea archetype uses a Mediterranean-type relation
components.source: Lee et al. (2006); marginal sea candidate: Schneider et al. (2007)

components.component: Precipitation-risk framework (NOT a single universal threshold)
components.formulation: Tiered, particle-context dependent: heterogeneous/particle-mediated risk range at roughly Omega_arag 4-7 (theta_het sampled 4-7 in Monte Carlo); pseudo-homogeneous nucleation range at roughly Omega_arag >= 10-12 (theta_hom sampled 10-12.5). Continuous index against both uncertain bounds plus flags precip_risk_het_flag and precip_risk_hom_flag and a documented particle_context assumption. The project never states that a given Omega value causes precipitation - only that a scenario enters a literature-derived, particle-context-dependent risk range
components.source: heterogeneous tier: Moras et al. (2022), Hartmann et al. (2023) - exact experimental ranges to verify; homogeneous tier: SOURCE VERIFICATION REQUIRED

components.formulation: solves for full carbonate speciation given any two of {TA, DIC, pH, pCO2}
independent bisection solver for [H+] built from the equations above, used for quality control
components.source: built for this project; validated against PyCO2SYS and published check values

validation_reference: Solver outputs are checked against the published reference values in Dickson, Sabine & Christian (2007), Guide to Best Practices for Ocean CO2 Measurements.
